title: Storage artifact policy & lifecycle orchestration for VPC Private Deployments
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a robust Terraform module and orchestration pattern for provisioning EBS, EFS, and S3 storage used by Private (VPC) deployments. The module must enforce account-safe defaults (encryption, lifecycle, immutability guards), provide snapshot and backup orchestration, and include preflight and runtime health checks plus documented upgrade paths for module version changes.
acceptance_criteria: Module provisions EBS volumes with CMK encryption by default and tags required by billing and audit teams
EFS mount targets created with security-group bindings suitable for private subnets and optional transit encryption
S3 buckets created with block public access, default encryption (KMS), object lock optional, lifecycle policies for snapshot/object retention configurable
Automated snapshot/backup orchestration: daily snapshots for EBS, incremental EFS backup via AWS Backup, and scheduled S3 object lifecycle/replication hooks
Terraform module exposes variables for kms_key_id, retention_days, snapshot_schedule_cron, cross_account_snapshot_role, and prevent_destroy toggle
Pre-flight validation script that checks for existing resources that would be impacted and outputs a migration plan (terraform import hints)
Health check CloudWatch metrics and a small Lambda probe (optionally deployed into customer account) that verifies snapshot age, encryption, and public access settings
Upgrade guide with documented Terraform state migration steps and a canary strategy for rolling upgrades across namespaces
Automated integration tests in CI that run against a sandbox account and validate module idempotency and destroy safety
technical_notes: Target providers: AWS provider >= 5.0. Use aws_kms_key with key_policy templated for cross-account snapshot roles. Prefer aws_ebs_encryption_by_default off + per-volume CMK for auditable key usage. For S3, use aws_s3control_bucket_ownership_controls where supported, and enable object lock via opt-in variable. Implement lifecycle using aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration and optional replication configuration for cross-region backups.
implementation_plan: Design module API and variables; gather input from Security and Billing
Prototype EBS sub-module with encryption, snapshot lifecycle, and import helpers
Implement EFS sub-module with access_points option and backup plan integration
Implement S3 sub-module with encryption, public-blocks, lifecycle, and optional object-lock
Add preflight Terraform plan analyzer (Python script) to detect destructive diffs and provide import suggestions
Add healthcheck Lambda + small Terraform blueprint to deploy probes in customer VPCs
Write CI integration tests and run against sandbox; iterate on failures
Prepare docs and upgrade guide; submit for security review
Ship module to internal registry and announce with migration instructions
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate + tflint + checkov on module
Integration: deploy module to sandbox account; verify resource creation, encryption, and lifecycle policies
Upgrade test: create resources with v1.0.0 then apply v1.1.0 with state-migration steps; confirm no data loss
Failure scenarios: simulate KMS key missing, insufficient IAM permissions, and enforce graceful error messages
Healthcheck failure: ensure alert triggers when latest snapshot > retention threshold
rollout_plan: Release to internal registry as v1.0.0 in canary mode for two pilot customers
Collect metrics for snapshot success rate and CI-run idempotency over 2 weeks
If stable, publish recommendation template in Private Deploy onboarding docs and run opt-in migrations with Solutions Engineering
For customers with heavy state, schedule assisted migration windows and use terraform import helpers
risks: KMS cross-account key policies are complex; misconfiguration can block snapshots or create data access issues
prevent_destroy defaults could block urgent maintenance if not well-documented
Large EFS/EBS estates mean terraform runs may time out; need provider-level timeouts and batching
Object lock and immutability can create irreversible states; must surface opt-in clearly
Upgrading module defaults (e.g., changing lifecycle rules) may require data retention legal review
decisions: Use CMK per-environment (not account-wide default) to allow customer key rotation without affecting other tenants
Expose prevent_destroy as opt-in variable but default it to true for production module outputs
Provide a lightweight healthcheck probe instead of depending solely on customer's monitoring stack to ensure consistent signals
Implement import-helper CLI (python) to generate terraform import commands for existing resources instead of performing blind imports in module code
